source.ref: Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, Sch. Art. 28 (family gift amounts subst. by Act 07 of 2016 w.e.f. 1-4-2016)
source.quoted_text: Sch Art. 28 (both columns, official DPAL text): 'Gift-instrument of, not being a settlement (No.48) or will or transfer (No.52) — (a) Where the donee is NOT a family member of the donor — The same duty as a Conveyance (Article No. 20) for a market value equal to the market value of the property. (b) Where the donee IS a member of the family of the donor — (i) if the property is situated within the limits of Bangalore Metropolitan Regional Development Authority or Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike or City Corporation — Rupees five thousand; (ii) if within City or Town Municipal Council or Town Panchayat area — Rupees three thousand; (iii) if within limits other than (i) and (ii) — Rupees one thousand; Provided that, if the property is situated in any combination of the said limits, the duty shall be the maximum of those.' Explanation: 'Family in relation to the donor for this purpose means father, mother, husband, wife, son, daughter, daughter-in-law, brothers, sisters and grand children.'

pending_verification.reason: Karnataka gift totals have unresolved surcharge scope: the 10% infrastructure duty may also apply to fixed family-gift duty, and the local-body surcharge instrument scope has not been established. Refuse both family and non-family gift totals until those primary provisions are sourced.

notes_for_reviewer: CONFIDENCE: HIGH (official DPAL text, both columns). The PRD §5.5 per-state relative-list showcase — and DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT from Maharashtra's: KA family gift is a FIXED area-based amount (Rs 5,000 BBMP/BMRDA/City Corp; Rs 3,000 Town Municipal/Panchayat; Rs 1,000 elsewhere), and KA's family list (father/mother/husband/wife/son/daughter/DAUGHTER-IN-LAW/brothers/sisters/grand children) differs from MH's — proof that generalizing a 'family' list would be a silent correctness bug. gift_relation_ka: 'family' → area-based fixed; else → conveyance rate (5% via cross-ref) + s.3B cess. The cross_ref to conveyance imports Art 20's CHARGE only (not its cess modifier); this rule's own KA-infra-cess-gift adds the 10% cess for non-family gifts. Family-gift cess treatment PENDING (see cess modifier notes). area_type shared with conveyance.
